# Experimental public projection/input fixtures

Hand-authored synthetic N0-06 data for [issue 12's public contract](../../../docs/engine/native-contract.md#n0-06-experimental-public-projections-and-intents), drafted 2026-10-16. Rust owns the DTOs; generated schemas and TypeScript types use `namtab.native.experimental.n0` / `n0-06-draft-1`. Existing public-v1, EA1 and older fixture bytes are preserved. These new review bounds and profile records are **proposals**, not owner-accepted production limits or an implemented API.

- `examples.json` contains independently considered candidate envelopes, a two-page immutable active-grid snapshot, one exact-base delta, correlated opening/refusal controls, read/credit/cancel/resume/active-unavailable shapes, per-fact trust levels and separate UI commands. Two concurrent same-projection starts have distinct correlations and stream IDs; zero-credit opening/grant/cancel and initial refusal are represented without a first page. Reused input sequence1 is deliberate fixture reuse, not a valid batch under one issued namespace. The old finite receipt model has only a 1024-byte body budget; the independent input candidates name an unaccepted `public-input-fixture-proposal` and claim no admission.
- `intent-cases.json` gives both-client edits to named examples. Only `expected_shape` is executed by strict Ajv tests. Every `semantic_expectation`, `expected_hex`, host event, mode/focus assumption and refusal rule is review data for independent future oracles. Native agents use the same explicit logical intent shapes with the direct-session route. No encoder, currentness/grant checker, application or frontend runs here.
- `subscription-cases.json` gives unexecuted immutable assembly, range completeness, credit, gap/resync, cancellation/disconnect and recovery-negative requirements. Its example references are checked for existence; the sequences are not executed. New requirements cover zero-credit control allowance, reversed openings for concurrent identical selections, initial refusal versus active unavailability, duplicate correlations and rejection of old-connection responses.

Static Node/Rust tests require correlation and resolved stream binding fields on opening/refusal/unavailability shapes; Node fixture assertions verify the synthetic mappings without executing a subscriber. The static Node suite compiles the generated JSON Schema with existing strict Ajv, validates all examples/edited variants, checks optional absent-versus-false/null, and demonstrates schema-valid semantic violations. Rust tests verify DTO round trips, namespace isolation, optional fact decoding, duplicate known input fields and raw unknown/duplicate-unknown fields on the three empty tagged projection/default-color/direct-session variants. Paired Ajv variants reject the same extra-field shapes; parsed-value validation cannot preserve raw duplicate keys. Schemars limits are schema metadata: Serde alone does not enforce them. Parsed-value schema validation cannot detect duplicate raw keys, authenticate a producer, establish u64 range/currentness, count UTF-8 budgets, apply a delta, consume credit or authorize a write. In particular, schema-valid stale-focus/input, counter overflow, wrong row width and 8194-byte text remain refused **requirements**, not passed runtime tests.

All IDs, text, application hints, clocks and control-looking strings are invented here; no captured transcripts, credentials, real prompts, environment values, private paths, upstream code or upstream fixture data are included. Authoring helpers only composed literal JSON; no embedded content was executed. `manifest.json` records local SHA-256 integrity, provenance, R10/R16 and V10/V16/DF01–DF04 mappings. It does not replace the original shared fixture manifest, alter historical X4/EA1 failures, add licensing or claim compatibility, performance, NG0 or N1 acceptance. Independent oracle review, production limit selection, transport/semantic validation and both-client implementation remain open.
